title: Forward queued reversals without holding up the transaction

blocks.text: When the Visa host doesn't answer, a participant writes a reversal to the `reversal.visa` queue of the Space and lets the transaction finish. `ReversalForwarder` gets each reversal from there to the link's sender, which talks to the host and can take several seconds per message. In production two forwarders listen to the same queue, one for each of the link's two channels.

items: every reversal written to the queue reaches a sender, and goes to the host once, not once per forwarder;
a reversal that has been handed to a sender is no longer in the queue;
the participant that queued a reversal gets on with its transaction while the host is still answering.

blocks.text: About three lines. The tests hold the host's answer with a latch in one of them.

cases.says: every reversal written to the queue reaches the sender
the listener runs on the writer's thread, so the slow send goes to a thread of its own
a notification does not remove the entry; the forwarder takes it
with two forwarders on one queue only the one whose take succeeded sends, so each reversal goes out once

origin.section: 12.4 A Listener Runs on the Writer's Thread and Takes Nothing

concepts: A listener runs on the writer's thread and does not take the entry: slow work goes to another thread, and a consumer takes with inp and accepts null.
